Today we will start with a piece of C++ source code and look at how the Clang front end understands a program. We will distinguish three concepts: the parser, the abstract syntax tree, and semantic analysis. They work together, but solve different problems.

The parser recognizes the syntactic structure of the code and builds an AST in cooperation with semantic analysis. The AST represents declarations, expressions, and statements as nodes. Having a syntactic structure does not mean a program is valid; types and the meaning of names still need to be checked.

Sema participates in name lookup, type checking, and diagnostics. For example, when the types in an expression do not match, the context is needed to understand the problem and produce a diagnostic. It is useful to study syntax and semantic constraints separately, but they should not be mistaken for two entirely isolated processing steps.

After front-end checks, code generation lowers the program to LLVM IR. Subsequent optimization operates on that intermediate representation. Today the focus is on component responsibilities and how they connect; specific optimization algorithms can be explored in a later session.
